Question B-007-002-007.

Why the correct answer is right: After a full night without sunlight, recombination has had the longest time to reduce ionization. That makes the period just before dawn the usual daily minimum.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Just after noon": Just after noon is near the daily solar-radiation maximum, not the ionization minimum.
- sourceIndex 2: "Just after dusk": Just after dusk is early in the nighttime decay; ionization has not usually reached its lowest point yet.
- sourceIndex 3: "Shortly before midnight": Shortly before midnight is dark, but it is not as late in the recombination period as the time before sunrise.
